issues.legal_issue: A review petition based on newly discovered evidence is maintainable only when the evidence was unavailable despite due diligence, is material to the decision under review, and could have altered that decision; review cannot be used to rehear the merits or substitute appellate reasoning.

The filing of a civil-contempt petition must occur within one year of the alleged contempt, and a party cannot obtain condonation of delay under the general provision for that purpose, although exemption from limitation may be available in an appropriately pleaded and established case.

A continuing breach for purposes of exemption from the limitation period for contempt requires a pleaded and established continuing breach of a continuing duty; continuing effects of a completed act of disobedience do not constitute a continuing breach.
A contempt court must confine its inquiry to deliberate disobedience of the order alleged to have been breached and cannot adjudicate title or other issues beyond the scope of that order.
